title: THE WEEK IN ANIME: POWER UNDER PRESSURE

scenes.narration: Talks without a deal. An election without a majority. Families escaping through a temporary ceasefire. And an AI boom facing an expensive question: when does the spending pay off? Five stories. One turbulent week. This is the world in anime.

scenes.chapter: The Gulf: a proposal, not a deal
scenes.narration: We start in the Gulf, where diplomacy continued under the threat of renewed strikes. On Sunday, Iranian negotiators were in Doha for talks with Qatari mediators, seeking a way to end the war involving Iran, the United States and Israel. Iran’s foreign minister described a proposal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days of a possible agreement with Washington. But he said no final agreement had been reached. The shipping route remains central to the negotiations. For now, the diplomatic breakthrough is still a possibility—not an announced outcome.

scenes.narration: In Israel, the votes are counted. Forming a government is the next battle. Results released on Friday gave Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc fifty-three seats. The main opposition bloc took forty-eight. Arab-led parties held nineteen. For an outright majority, the target is sixty-one seats in the one-hundred-and-twenty-seat parliament. Netanyahu remains prime minister while parties try to build a coalition. Those nineteen seats do not automatically belong to either main bloc. The election is over. The struggle to turn votes into a governing majority continues.

scenes.narration: Now to Ukraine, where this week brought a narrow opening for civilians. On Saturday, evacuees from Russian-occupied Oleshky reached Ukrainian-held territory and reunited with relatives. Their route ran through Russia and Belarus, under a local ceasefire that also allowed humanitarian aid. That pause began on Tuesday and was scheduled to end on Sunday evening. It covered a limited area. Fighting continued elsewhere in Ukraine. The wider war went on. But for families arriving at the border, the week brought something immediate: getting out, reaching safety, finding each other.

scenes.narration: In France, the pressure moved onto the streets. Saturday brought a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations over living costs and education. Authorities estimated three-hundred-and-twenty-thousand participants across the country. Organizers put the number higher. Most people marched peacefully. Later clashes involving smaller groups broke out in Paris and other cities. The movement’s demands have broadened to include civil liberties and the right to protest. The crowds filled the streets. The political questions behind the protests remained unresolved.

scenes.chapter: Markets: the cost of the AI race
scenes.narration: Across the Atlantic, confidence came under pressure on the trading screens. On Friday, the S and P five hundred fell one-point-eight percent. The Nasdaq Composite dropped two-point-nine percent. Technology shares led the sell-off as disappointing earnings and concerns about huge AI investments unsettled investors. The question is becoming harder to dodge: how much of that spending will turn into financial returns? The AI race carries enormous expectations. This week, Wall Street delivered a reminder that expectations still have to survive an earnings report.
